summary: Added a tabbed Settings page for myiotsan (`apps/myiotsan/views/react-webpack/src/views/components/settings.js`) consolidating everything that configures the hub itself -- Users, Location, Notifications, Telemetry, Connectivity, System -- behind one admin-only nav entry, backed by two new runtime-editable settings stores and a system-restart endpoint. `services.NotificationSettingsService` (new `apps/myiotsan/services/notification_settings.go`) persists a webhook/telegram delivery config as a JSON blob in the shared RuntimeSetting KV and, critically, is the FIRST code path in the app that ever calls the shared `notification.Service.Configure` -- before this change myiotsan wrote every alert only to its in-app feed regardless of any config, because nothing wired the shared outbound delivery engine (webhook POST / Telegram bot API, unmodified shared infra) up at all. Saving from the Notifications tab (`GET/PUT /api/settings/notification`, `POST /api/settings/notification/test`) now applies the config to the live hub immediately, and a `Sync` call at boot re-applies a previously-saved config to each fresh process. `services.TelemetrySettingsService` (new `apps/myiotsan/services/telemetry_settings.go`) persists raw/rollup retention days, write-batcher batch size/flush interval/queue size, and the embedded MQTT broker's listen address (`GET/PUT /api/settings/telemetry`), seeded from `config.json` defaults the first time; `app.go` now reads this store's effective value once at boot (store-over-config) to size `NewReadingWriter`, `telemetry.RunRollup`, and `iotmqtt.New`, replacing direct `config.json` reads at those three call sites -- an edit here does not apply live and needs a restart, which the tab states plainly and links to. A new `apps/myiotsan/apis/system.go` (`NewSystemApi`) adds `POST /api/system/restart` (admin-only, responds 200 before restarting ~500ms later via the shared apphost.Restarter) to make that restart reachable from inside the app. The RBAC catalog (`apps/myiotsan/services/rbac.go`) gained explicit admin-only rows for `/api/settings/notification`, `/api/settings/telemetry`, and `/api/system`, and separately closed a pre-existing gap found alongside this work: `/api/pairing` (fleet key, claim code, adoption status) had never been listed in the catalog at all. The existing site-location panel moved from the Schedules page into the new Settings page (Location tab) with no backend change. Verified live end to end on a booted app: created a user and assigned it a role, set the site location, saved and test-fired a webhook (confirmed delivery was actually configured), saved telemetry retention (confirmed unedited fields kept their defaults), read pairing status, and read version/health.
compatibility: Backward-compatible for every existing install: both settings blobs default to safe values (notification channels disabled; telemetry defaults taken from the existing config.json values) when no row has ever been saved, so an upgrade changes no runtime behavior until an admin explicitly opts in from the new Settings page. Existing `/api/settings/users`/`/api/settings/roles` behavior is unchanged. The one-time cost: an admin who wants outbound delivery or changed storage/broker settings must visit the new page and save; telemetry/broker edits additionally require a restart (via the new System tab) to take effect, since those values are still read only at process construction.
